title: Territory Lockbox: Operational Notes for Interim Residency Enforcement
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an operational pattern we’re calling the \"Territory Lockbox\" — a temporary, auditable holding state for tenant data when requested region pinning cannot be satisfied immediately (capacity, legal review, or integrations). Goal is to provide a low-risk, transparent way to satisfy customer commitments while we complete full-region onboarding or document exceptions with legal.

Scope and when to use
- Use for enterprise customers with explicit region/residency contract language when the target anchor region is not available at activation time.
- NOT intended for long-term storage (>90 days) unless escalated to legal + product for contract amendment.
- Intended as an operator-facing containment + evidence-capture pattern to be used only with documented customer consent.

High level pattern
1) Quarantine: Route all new tenant writes to a locked, encrypted bucket/container tagged with the customer territory and a lockbox identifier. No cross-region replication.
2) Evidence capture: Every write has an accompanying signed assertion (metadata) containing timestamp, operator-id, customer consent reference (ticket id/contract clause), and the reason for lockbox.
3) Temporal routing: Reads remain available from the lockbox if customer allows; otherwise reads are proxied to token-limited service endpoint.
4) Migration path: When region is provisioned or exception approved, run a managed migration with audit records and customer notification.

Operator checklist (quick)
- [ ] Confirm customer consent exists (ticket # or legal-approved clause).
- [ ] Create lockbox ID in ops-tooling: lockbox-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.
- [ ] Provision non-replicated encrypted container in region-closest (per customer) host.
- [ ] Tag tenant resources: residency:lockbox, lockbox-id:<id>, lock-reason:<short>.
- [ ] Deploy circuit-breaker policy to prevent accidental cross-replication.
- [ ] Emit initial audit event: residency.lockbox.created (include operator, ticket, container, TTL).
- [ ] Notify customer and account team with template message.

Telemetry and evidence format (minimal fields we must capture)
- event_id: UUID (string)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- operator: <full name/email>
- tenant_id: <tenant id>
- lockbox_id: <string>
- reason_code: {CAPACITY|LEGAL_REVIEW|INTEGRATION_BLOCKER|OTHER}
- consent_reference: {ticket-###, contract-clause}
- container_path: s3://... or gs://...
- migration_plan_id: optional

Secure storage considerations
- Lockbox containers must be encrypted with a dedicated KMS key per customer (or tenant-group) when available. If KMS not available in chosen host region, use an encrypted vault with access logging and HSM-backed KEK in allowable region only after legal approval.
- No long-lived credentials: use short-lived role assumption for operator actions; require MFA for migration ops.

Migration procedure (happy path)
1) Validate target region readiness (capacity, network egress rules, KMS availability, compliance flags).
2) Schedule migration window with customer and operations calendar (min 72h notice).
3) Snapshot lockbox container, compute checksum manifests per shard.
4) Initiate one-way transfer to target region using S3 replication or secure transfer proxy with TLS + mTLS.
5) Rehydrate in target tenant environment, run integrity checks (checksums, record counts).
6) Switch tenant pin to target region (atomic operation controlled by feature flag).
7) Emit residency.lockbox.migrated and residency.pin.assigned events.
8) Retain pre-migration lockbox for N days (retention window declared to customer) then securely delete, recording deletion evidence.

Rollback and failure modes
- Partial copy: if checksum mismatch, mark migration as FAILED, revert reads to lockbox-only, escalate to SRE + se-ed for forensic copy.
- Target KMS mismatch: pause and request legal signoff for allowable interim key usage or delay migration.
- Customer withdraws consent mid-migration: pause, create incident, capture signed withdrawal and follow contract terms.

Operator commands (examples)
- Create lockbox container (internal tooling): ops lockbox create --tenant <TID> --region <region> --reason CAPACITY --ticket ENG-4123
- Tag tenant: ops tenant tag --tenant <TID> residency:lockbox=true lockbox-id=<id>
- Emit audit event: ops audit emit --event residency.lockbox.created --meta "{\"tenant\":\"<TID>\",\"lockbox\":\"<id>\"}"
- Start migration job: ops migration start --lockbox <id> --target-region eu-west-1 --plan <plan-id>

Customer communication templates (ops to send)
Subject: Temporary territory lockbox for <Tenant name> (region: <requested region>)
Body: Hi <Customer contact>,
As discussed, we’ve placed new traffic and data into a temporary lockbox while we finish provisioning <requested region> or finalize legal approvals. This is a temporary, non-replicated storage that preserves data locality and prevents cross-border transfer. We expect migration within X–Y days. Ticket: <ticket>. Please reply with confirmation to proceed.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Perception of non-compliance. Mitigation: Require explicit consent and include audit bundle in customer mailbox; provide clear deletion/migration timelines.
- Risk: Single-region outage impacts access. Mitigation: Allow operator-controlled read-proxy to degrade access gracefully; provide SLAs for lockbox-read latency.
- Risk: Accidental replication. Mitigation: Circuit-breaker flags and infra-level ACLs that disallow replication operations from lockbox containers.

Acceptance criteria for closing a lockbox (to be used by product/legal)
- Target region has been certified for customer’s jurisdiction and signed off by compliance.
- KMS and ingress/egress policies validated in target region.
- Migration completed with integrity proofs (checksums + record counts).
- Customer has acknowledged migration completion and post-migration retention window.
- Deletion evidence recorded for pre-migration lockbox.

Open questions / TODOs
- TTL policy: default 60 days vs. 90 days? Need legal guidance; for now set to 60 and escalate for long durations.
- Audit schema: do we standardize the event envelope across all residency docs? Proposal: yes, file a small RFC.
- Billing implications: how do we reflect lockbox storage/egress in customer billing? Finance to advise.

Appendix: sample audit event (raw)
{
  "event_id": "c9f1d4a6-2f3b-4c3d-8aef-123456789abc",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-20T15:22:10Z",
  "operator": "Aisha Kapoor <aisha@redwood.ai>",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-4932",
  "lockbox_id": "lockbox-tenant-4932-20250220",
  "reason_code": "CAPACITY",
  "consent_reference": "TICKET-9811",
  "container_path": "s3://eu-temp-lockboxes/lockbox-tenant-4932-20250220"
}

Notes to future reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight (operator-first) and does not replace the full residency enforcement product. Treat as temporary stopgap.
- When we iterate, fold evidence schema into the central residency-event service and add runbook-driven automation for creation and migration to reduce manual error.

Revision history
- 2024-11-14: Draft created by Aisha K. initial pattern and checklist.
- 2025-01-09: Added migration procedure and telemetry fields (Benji M).
- 2025-02-20: Clarified KMS guidance and added acceptance criteria (Claire J).
